answer.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing is the most acute threat to SMB share right now, and memory_73 directly claims promotional pricing works for price-sensitive SMBs with acquisition and revenue lift. But the memory record only speaks to acquisition/time-to-value, not to churn quality or long-term margin/retention of price-sensitive cohorts—exactly the risk that matters given our objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so I want to see the original experiment record before committing at any scale beyond a guarded test. I also want to verify memory_31 (signup simplification) since onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter and a lower-risk, already-validated activation-side fix could be a safer use of this week's single experiment slot if the pricing evidence turns out thin or short-horizon. Given only one experiment slot and a live competitive threat, I'm leaning toward testing promotional pricing but only as a small guarded test with explicit tracking of downstream retention/margin, not a broad rollout, until the archived record confirms the lift is durable and not just a short-term acquisition spike.
